newsitem.title: USA: IATA to study how to store perishables on aircraft.
newsitem.headline: IATA to study how to store perishables on aircraft.

text.p: The International Air Transport Association is working on a computer mapping project to help air carriers of perishables, an IATA executive told Reuters.
"We are developing a computer program to determine which is the best location for each type of perishable commodity," Joseph Chan, IATA manager of special cargos said Friday.
Chan is working with Airbus Industrie and Laval University, Quebec City, on the project, which will map products based on temperature and humidity.

Perishables generate heat, condensation and gasses as they are stored. The condensation can cause false fire alarms on aircraft, Chan said. In one case, the false alarm prompted an emergency landing and caused some passenger injuries.
"The purpose of the mapping is to help eliminate this kind of problem," he said. The mapping will also maximize the use of capacity on the aircraft.
Chan hopes to have a prototype available for Airbus for trial by the summer. He hopes Boeing will join the project and that by year-end, IATA would have a program for Boeing Co, too.
Chan could not estimate how much the programs might cost. He hopes to make them available on the Internet.
